q2_gaps: "become" plus a predicative complement (a change-of-state copular verb) - "Two kinds of clause" splits only copular "is" from ordinary verbal clauses and gives no shape for the resulting predication; the parse borrowed the resultative shape (Patient subject + reified state + flat atom + Result), which is analogous but not licensed anywhere as such

attributive "once ADJ" (formerly ADJ, inside the NP) - the Past wrapper is only specified for a past-tense copular clause or an appositive under one, and the cessation cue list ("no longer / not anymore / used to") does not include "once", so the implication that the relationship is no longer strategic has no representation
a two-argument "between X and Y" post-modifier on an entity noun - the instruction set illustrates entity-attached prepositions only for the one-argument "from" case
notes: The sentence-medial "now" before the perfect auxiliary is treated exactly as an adverb of the become event, which is the reading the instruction set's deictic-constant rule gives. Between is entity-attached rather than event-attached, exemplified only for From, but it is the preposition actually used so it stays inside the open-class oblique licence.
